viper.name: NASA VIPER (Volatiles Investigating Polar Exploration Rover)

track_width_m.src: ~1.3 m at nominal ride height, Schepelmann et al. 2025

psr_ops_limit_h.src: batteries sized for 9 h shadowed operations

cg_height_m.src: centre-of-mass height not published; assumed 0.75 m (body + mast)

drive_efficiency.src: motor x gearbox x electronics efficiency, not published

hotel_power_w.src: calibrated so a flat drive at nominal speed exhausts 5420 Wh in the published 9 h PSR limit

battery_reserve_frac.src: operational reserve not published; 10 % kept in reserve

max_slip_ops.src: slip-sinkage expected to be controlled under 40 % slip, Schepelmann et al. 2025

references: Bluethmann, VIPER Rover Overview and Mobility and Hardware, LSIC 2024-11-14 (docs/references/viper_lsic2024_mobility_hw.pdf)
Schepelmann et al. 2025, PSJ, VIPER mobility (docs/references/viper_mobility_psj2025.pdf)

perseverance.name: Perseverance-class rover (NASA Mars 2020) on the Moon — hypothetical

n_wheels.src: six wheels, each with its own motor

grouser_height_m.src: 48 grousers published; height not published (Curiosity-like 7.5 mm assumed)

track_width_m.src: front/rear wheel-centre spacing measured from NASA 3D model

wheelbase_m.src: front-to-rear wheel-centre distance measured from NASA 3D model

wheel_positions_m.src: wheel centres (forward, left) measured from NASA 3D model, relative to wheel centroid

steer_range_deg.src: corner-wheel steering; range not on the NASA page

speed_nominal_mps.src: top speed 152 m/h on flat hard ground (NASA); used as commanded speed

max_slope_req_deg.src: drivers avoid terrain tilting the rover > 30 deg (NASA)

battery_wh.src: two Li-ion batteries; capacity not published

solar_peak_w.src: no solar arrays; MMRTG ~110 W at launch (NASA)

psr_ops_limit_h.src: not qualified for lunar PSR; no limit applied

cg_height_m.src: from the published 45 deg tilt rating: h = half-track(1.062 m) / tan 45

references: NASA 3D Resources: Mars 2020 Perseverance Rover.glb (github.com/nasa/NASA-3D-Resources); geometry measured in metres, wheel diameter 0.525 m matches the published 52.5 cm
perseverance.fidelity_warning: Hypothetical: Perseverance is a Mars rover. Its mass, wheels, speed, tilt rating and MMRTG power are NASA-published, and its wheel layout is measured from NASA's to-scale 3D model. It was never qualified for lunar PSR temperatures, and battery capacity is not published, so no shadow-time or battery limit is applied. Mobility and stability results are physically meaningful; endurance is not modelled.

pragyan.name: ISRO Pragyan (Chandrayaan-3 rover)

n_wheels.src: six-wheel rocker-bogie per ISRO imagery; not in the spec table

body_length_m.src: commonly reported 917 mm; not on ISRO spec page

speed_nominal_mps.src: ~1 cm/s widely reported; not on ISRO spec page

max_slip_ops.src: same operational threshold as VIPER, assumed

references: ISRO Chandrayaan-3 mission details: rover mass 26 kg, power 50 W, communicates only with lander, one lunar day
pragyan.fidelity_warning: ISRO publishes only mass, power and mission life for the rover. Wheel geometry, speed, dimensions and battery are NOT officially published, so this profile is low-fidelity. LGI trafficability studies (Carrier) also show the Apollo-era Bekker model under-predicts difficulty for small rover wheels. Results are indicative only. Pragyan was not designed for PSRs, and it relays through its lander (range-limited).

apollo_lrv_nominal.name: Lunar regolith — Apollo LRV design values
apollo_lrv_nominal.src: Costes, Farmer & George (1972) Mobility performance of the Lunar Roving Vehicle; Carrier (1991) Lunar Sourcebook ch. 9; as quoted in Carrier, LGI 'Trafficability of lunar microrovers' Part 1 (docs/references/lgi_trafficability_part1.pdf)

loose_psr_hypothetical.name: Loose/low-strength regolith (sensitivity case, hypothetical)
loose_psr_hypothetical.src: Sensitivity case only: phi lowered to 30 deg (lower bound of the Apollo 30-50 deg range, Connolly & Carrier LPSC 2023), cohesion and moduli halved. NOT a measured PSR soil.
